title: Add one link back. How big is the core?
hook: One new link runs from OUT back to IN. How many pages join the core?

knows: links between web pages are one-way
the IN / core / OUT picture of the web (web-bow-tie-reach)
doesNotKnow: that one new link from OUT back to IN joins exactly the pages on the loop it closes, not the whole of IN and OUT

misconception: One link from OUT back to IN pulls all of IN and OUT into the core.
objective: The learner can say that a new link from an OUT page back to an IN page adds to the core only the pages on the loop it closes (here E, F, H and I, making 8), because a page joins the core only when it can both reach the core and be reached from it.

claims.text: In the stage graph (links A→B, B→C, C→D, D→A, E→A, F→E, G→B, C→H, H→I, D→J) the core, the pages that each reach every other, is A to D (4 pages). Adding I → F closes the loop F → E → A → B → C → H → I → F and makes the core A to F, H and I (8 pages); G still cannot be reached from the core and J cannot reach it, so both stay out. Adding J → G instead closes J → G → B → C → D → J and gives A to D, G and J (6 pages); adding both links gives all 10.
claims.source: Node reachability both ways over the exact edge list in Demo.tsx (coreOf(): pages A reaches that also reach A). Builder ran it 2026-10-22: {"before":[A,B,C,D],"addIF":[A,B,C,D,E,F,H,I],"addJG":[A,B,C,D,G,J],"both":[all 10]}; every other page is its own group in each case. Before: pages reaching A = A–G, pages A reaches = A–D, H, I, J. Matches the brief's check J5.

claims.text: A page belongs to the core (the same strongly connected group) exactly when it can reach the core and the core can reach it, following links the way they point.
claims.source: Definition of a strongly connected component; Easley and Kleinberg, Networks, Crowds, and Markets (2010), ch. 13 (section unconfirmed, brief says 13.3–13.4).

claims.text: A new link from an OUT page u back to an IN page v adds to the core exactly the pages on a loop through the new link (the pages v reaches that also reach u), not every IN and OUT page. On the stage each added link closes one such loop.
claims.source: From c2: the core reaches u and v reaches the core, so with u → v a page w joins exactly when it lies on core ⇝ u → v ⇝ core, i.e. v ⇝ w ⇝ u. Node check 2026-10-22 on the stage graph: rule(I→F) = A–F, H, I; rule(J→G) = A–D, G, J, equal to c1.

claims.text: The 10-page web on the stage is a toy, not to scale (reveal: "A toy web, not to scale.").
claims.source: Disclosure that the stage is a teaching model, not crawl data.

recall.question: A web has a core, IN pages that link into it and OUT pages it links to. You add one link from an OUT page back to an IN page. Which pages join the core?
options: Only the two pages the link joins
The pages on the loop the new link closes
recall.why: A page joins the core only if it can reach the core and the core can reach it. The new link gives that only to the pages on a loop through it.
